cast.characterName: メル・ファン・デ・グラーフ
cast.originalCharacterName: メル・ファン・デ・グラーフ

segments.text: A passenger in a third-class hard seat car.
She is Charlotte's maid and the daughter of a good family with ties to a family of witches. Despite her connection, Mel has no magical powers.

The political situation between the two countries and the empire has become unstable, and popular fear of a return of the nightmare of the previous war has triggered a medieval-like witch hunt. Mel jumps on a train to protect Charlotte, who is on her way to escape to her aunt's house.

She is extremely polite, intelligent, and erudite. She is certified as a nurse so that if and when Charlotte, who is sickly and frail, is in danger, she can be treated appropriately. While Charlotte acts with sensitivity, Mel always confronts things with logic.
At the age of 13, Mel came to Charlotte's house not as a maid, but as an apprentice to train to be a bride. She's aware of the circumstances of Charlotte's magical powers.

Although her term of service has already expired, she has become so attached to Charlotte that she continues to serve as her maid to this day. She has feelings for Charlotte, who only allows herself to be loved by her outside of the family, similar to those of her own sister, and she is determined to continue to serve her until Charlotte meets a man of her dreams.

The children's books that Charlotte loves to read originally belonged to Mel. She is surprisingly athletic and carries a P08 modified Baby Luger pistol hidden away so that she can eliminate any threat to Charlotte at a moment's notice.

cast.characterName: リットマイスター・ワインバーガー・フライヘル・フォン・ミケシュ
cast.originalCharacterName: リットマイスター・ワインバーガー・フライヘル・フォン・ミケシュ

segments.text: Conductor. President of the International Sleeping Car Company, an elderly gentleman with a calm demeanor.
He was a knight heard in the last war. He and his beloved grandchildren are on board the Magic Arrow, the maiden train of the "Trans-European Express" project, which has just been completed.
He loves his only family member, his granddaughter Milch, and is taking good care of her. Although he raised a son before, this is her first time raising a girl, so it's a little awkward...

Weinberger had a son who was to become his successor, but he and his wife were killed in an accident two years ago, leaving the young Milch behind. The son and his wife were on a trip to inspect the railroads in the beaten path, and on their way home, the airliner they were boarding crashed on level ground just as it was about to land at the airfield in their hometown where the father and his beloved daughter were picking them up. All the passengers and crew on board were killed.
The "Trans-European Express" project was, so to speak, a gift to Weinberger's son and daughter-in-law. Rittmeister means "knight captain" and Freiherr means "baron". Von means "distinguished family.
Weinberger carries a Dillinger as a self-defense pistol, perhaps out of pride as a knight or to protect his granddaughter.
Passenger in first class noontime car.

Granddaughter of Weinberger. At the age of four, while being carried in her grandfather's arms, she witnessed a passenger plane crash in front of her. As a young child, Milch was unable to understand that her parents were on the plane and that they would not return.　Later, as Weinberger raised her with great care and respect, his grandfather's attitude as he took care of her, and his refusal to tell her about her parents told her more eloquently about the reality of her situation, and now Milch is vaguely aware of her own circumstances.

She may be a young child, but she has a strong core and is compassionate. Just as Weinberger cares for her, Milch cares for her grandfather and cheers her up, even though he is probably more depressed than she is, through his everyday gestures.
On the Magic Arrow, Milch is dressed as Lucia, the star of Weinberger's Christmas event, wearing a pure white dress, a crimson belt, a crown of fir leaves and a candle flame.
She loves the starry sky, and when she spots the first twinkling star at night, she feels that it might be the lights of her parents' airliner.
First-class passenger
She is a secret agent of a certain agency in the Orient. She is on board the Magic Arrow to arrest a man.

She is a beautiful woman with long, shiny hair as black as the starry sky, braided in a careless manner, and dressed in men's clothes. She is dressed as a man because it is more convenient for her to act as a man on this mission. It is not that she has any strange hobbies. When the nature of the task at hand dictates that it would be easier for her to move around in her female form, she reverts to her original glamorous appearance.

However, whether in male or female form, her neat facial features and soft speech give a neutral impression to the other party. ...She is not emotionless, but she is not good at expressing her feelings honestly.
She is skilled in the special technique of using familiar objects as weapons, and in close combat, he uses his pigtails to strangle his target.

Thetrain carries a man who may be the target. The mission is a battle for authority between bureaucrats everywhere, involving opium and money. Akutagawa understands that she is merely a pawn in a political game and, with a kind of resigned calm, never takes rash action beyond his means. Although she and the target man she's chasing are acquaintances, they share a strange sense of solidarity and trust. She carries a Walther Kamp pistol. She is divorced.
A passenger of the first class nocturnal car.
He is an opium trafficker employed by a public agency that is in conflict with an agency in an Oriental country.
He is on board the Magic Arrow to smuggle Persian red opium, a high-quality opium.
When the train departs on time after confirming that Akutagawa is on board, it is safe to say that Chen's goal has been achieved.

He had no intention of succeeding in smuggling opium, and he was the one who tipped off the agency about the opium smuggling route being developed on the Trans-Europe Express. The bait was himself. The Agency will surely appoint Akutagawa to the position. However, he is retiring, not turning himself in, and has no intention of being arrested and detained.

For what it's worth, Chen is a softie. He is stingy with small change, but not with large sums of money. He has a childish side, with a fondness for dried potatoes. He always wears a smile as if he can see right through people's hearts, or in other words, like Akutagawa, he has no facial expression. He is reluctant to reveal his true feelings and acts in an almost dehumanizing manner. He carries a small spinning top as a good-luck charm.
He is divorced. He carries a Hino Komuro-style automatic pistol and is an expert sniper.

cast.characterName: マリーン・デートリッヒ
cast.originalCharacterName: マリーン・デートリッヒ

segments.text: Passenger in the first-class coach.
She is on the luxury express train, the Magic Arrow, with her fiancé, Francis, who is younger than her.
Until a few years ago, she was performing in small theaters while studying hard to become an actress, but she realized her lack of talent, gave up on her dream, and started running a small bar.

Although she has given up on her dream, she has not abandoned it. She'd be lying if she said she had no regrets, but she tried to play many different characters, and now that she has a job that allows her to interact with many different people, she feels that her life is worth living.

In fact, she has been married once. She was married to an older musician, Val, whom she met when she was an actress, but he died of illness just two months after their marriage. Five years later, she finally recovered from the sorrow of bereavement and bought a ticket for a prenuptial trip with Francis, the love of her life, who is her new mutual support. However, that night, Val's ghost suddenly appears, stalks Marine, and begins to torment her about her marriage to Francis.

At first, she is surprised and thinks it is a hallucination, but the ghost shows no sign of disappearing. When Val appeared, Marlene was puzzled, angry, and reminiscing about the old days. For some reason, she can only see her late husband. She is the only one who can talk to him. Talking with Val, she feels refreshed and at peace. That's when she realized she was still in love with this man.

cast.characterName: フランシス・ボールドウィン
cast.originalCharacterName: フランシス・ボールドウィン

segments.text: A passenger in the first class noontime car.

Marine's fiancé, a young man who is a fledgling painter. Recently, his paintings have finally been recognized by the world and are starting to sell. He is a regular customer at Marine's bar, where his various paintings are displayed. He is a weak man, and has a completely different appearance and personality from that of Marine's late husband, and if he were dressed up as a woman, he would look like a beautiful girl.

He never loses her moderation and treats even his inferiors with politeness and courtesy. Sometimes to the dismay of others, Francis is not in the habit of enjoying making people feel threatened, but that is all he can do.

He has been a close friend of Marine and Anne since Val was still alive, but since that time, Francis' honest attitude has not changed at all. At best, he respects Marine, and at worst, he remains a stranger even after their engagement and marriage have been finalized. After the prenuptial trip was decided, he was puzzled by Marine's sudden announcement that Val had come back to him. Francis has no idea what is happening to her.

How is he supposed to handle his fiancée who suddenly starts laughing (at Val's jokes), getting furious (when Val tells her off about her second marriage), and crying (when she reminisces with Val) when she tries to get him to come to his senses?

Francis is gradually becoming confused by Marine, who happily talks about things that only she and Val know (because Val, the ghost, talked, of course), including the fact that the painting for which Francis was recognized by the world was inspired by Val's music....
Passenger of the first class noontime car.

A close friend of Marine's and a first-class dancer. She was Val's lover. She is a very strong-willed and auspicious woman. She is the opposite of the motherly Marine, but perhaps that is why they can be best friends.

She is fed up with being forced by Francis to accompany him on his prenuptial trip. A few days ago, Marine began to speak and act as if Val were right in front of her. Francis is half in a panic when he sees her like this, but Anne is not worried. Anne is not worried, because the Marine she sees now is exactly the same as she was when Val was alive.

For Anne, this trip was nothing more than an awkward lover's quarrel between the couple. She had been friends with Val before his death because of her work. She had a faint crush on Val, who entertained her with his witty banter, and once crossed the line and slept with him. Although Anne did not tell Marine, Val was quite a playboy before his death. Anne was not the only one he had affairs with.
If, indeed, Val's ghost exists, it must be stalking Marine with a mixture of good and bad intentions. Anne, as Marine's best friend, is angry with Val for coming back now.

cast.characterName: バレンタイン・ジーバー
cast.originalCharacterName: バレンタイン・ジーバー

segments.text: Passenger(?) of the first class noontime car.

He was Marine's husband and an excellent musician. Val is a serious man at heart, but he is a womanizer and a jovial man who takes advantage of his title as a musician. Although he does not tell Marine, he played with quite a few women before his death, and even had his way with Anne, Marine's best friend. But it is also true that he loved Marine.
Perhaps Val understands Marine better than Marine herself. He must have understood why he had become a ghost.

Why did he have to come back from heaven? Marrying someone new would be a betrayal of her late husband... a betrayal of him, a forgetting of him. I guess that's what Marine believes. To rebuke Marine, Val is on board the Magic Arrow. And it is also for Francis.

cast.characterName: ソーミャン・リッベントロップ
cast.originalCharacterName: ソーミャン・リッベントロップ

segments.text: Passenger of the first class coach.

She was born into a wealthy family. Her father's business has failed and the family has been separated. Somian is unable to do anything about her unfortunate situation, but she does not lament her circumstances. Her family has been broken up, but she is not bereft.

She will work to help others, save money, and one day build a small house and bring her family over. We will not be as wealthy as before, but we will live together again. With this one thought in mind, Somian is living well.

She saw a poster on a street corner that advertised for "military nurses," and was attracted by the picture of a neat and clean nurse and the type of work she could do, so she applied for the job. If she became a military nurse, the government would take care of her food, clothing, and shelter, and she would earn a salary and be able to help many people.

Now, Somian is traveling on the Magic Arrow, accompanied by Eino, the examiner, to the examination center to take the exam to become a nurse at the Red Cross Hospital. Somian boards the train almost fully clothed, but she wears around her neck as a treasured pendant a "dream catcher" amulet that her mother bought for her on a trip abroad when her family was wealthy.

cast.characterName: エイノ・チェンバレン
cast.originalCharacterName: エイノ・チェンバレン

segments.text: A passenger in the first-class coach.
At first glance, he appears to be an ordinary mature man, but in reality, he is a trafficker for an underground organization that pimps out comfort women to brothels in the war zones.

When he tries to recruit comfort women by pretending to be a nurse in a fake "recruitment for military nurses," usually, a whore who knows the situation applies for the job, but very rarely, a girl with a clean body like Somian arrives. Of course, they may be mistaken. However, amateur girls with little experience fetch a high price as they are reserved for officers. There is no way they would turn her away.
Eino tricks these unfortunate girls and takes them to a place far from their hometowns so that they can never escape by themselves, and turns them into high-class prostitutes for trafficking.

However, since inexperienced girls are not suitable as prostitutes, he forcibly commits adultery with them on the way to the destination. If the girl resists violently, he forcefully trains her, uses aphrodisiacs, and forces her to face the harsh reality of her situation.

Aside from the individual circumstances of the girls, there are many soldiers in the war zones who, under the influence of the fake posters, mistakenly believe that the nurses are comfort women, and this has become a problem.

There are real nurses in the war zone, and the Red Cross has complained about the fraudulent "recruitment of military nurses," and organizations in various countries have begun to take action to expose them, but the activities of the patching organizations are too sophisticated to fully grasp their true nature. The organization has a stick with a long, slender sword inside.

cast.characterName: エドマンド・ビグルスワーク
cast.originalCharacterName: エドマンド・ビグルスワーク

segments.text: Passenger of the first class noonday car.

He was royalty of the Duke's kingdom, but is now a city man, a marquis-turned-count, and works as a town doctor. In spite of this, he is wearing a coat of arms embroidered with the royal family's crest, a saber, a sign of knighthood, and spurred military boots, and is aboard the Magic Arrow.
Why is he silently claiming his royalty, which he himself should have renounced? Who is he claiming it for?

The day before Edmund purchased his express ticket, the Magic Arrow also had a strange configuration. The Trans-European Express is being built with the cooperation of a number of countries. At the request of one of these countries, the Empire, a luxury express train consisting of only power cars and first-class coach cars was to be coupled with a rugged freight car and a third-class hard-sided car.
The Doshisha and the Empire had a history of being embroiled in the last World War, when they became enemies of each other and engaged in warfare. The past is too recent to be called history.

Although diplomatic relations between the two countries have been restored, no formal ceasefire treaty has been signed, and in that sense, it is not the past but the present. And now, as just before the outbreak of the last war, the political situation has become unstable.

Under these circumstances, the Imperial intervention has resulted in a change in the vehicle fleet. Edmund, alone, bought a ticket on the Magic Arrow. Only the feelings behind Edmund's elegant smile can tell you what these signs mean. His hobby is calligraphy. He wears a pistol saber that has a strange and bizarre shape, a combination of a Borchardt automatic pistol and a Schweitzer saber.

cast.characterName: ダラディエ・アンテロ・ルーッカネン
cast.originalCharacterName: ダラディエ・アンテロ・ルーッカネン

segments.text: Passenger of the first class noontime car.

An officer of the Imperial Intelligence Service. The principle is that "an intelligence officer should not act like an intelligence officer. Loukkanen is a one-armed man who lost his left arm and his wife and child in an accident on a previous mission.

He wears a suit and a wooden prosthetic arm and hand, but because he stands out from normal people, Luukkanen acts like a normal person. However, he sometimes acts and speaks in a way that is out of character for ordinary people, and is even comical to the casual observer.

Although he has lost one of his arms, he still retains the warmth of a human being, not a soldier, and is considerate of his subordinates. However, he is extremely indifferent to his enemies. As an intelligence officer, he does not let his emotions get in the way of his judgment, and will not hesitate to attack obstacles if necessary to accomplish his mission.
The additional freight cars on the Magic Arrow are commanded by the Imperial Central Command, but the third-class hard seats are towed at the sole discretion of Luukkanen in the field.

This time, Luukkanen's mission is to guard the wagons to a certain point along the route and ensure the safety of the cargo without being noticed by the public. Luukkanen is not too keen on the details of this mission, as he respects the basic premise that transcends friend and foe: "Never get civilians involved".

He carries a Webley-Fosbury automatic revolver, which has been adopted as the standard armament of the Imperial Intelligence Service. The pistol was originally developed to be used with one hand, and Luukkanen has overcome the disadvantage of having only one arm. He is a good slip shooter and can fire accurately and quickly. He is also skilled in handling explosives in general.

First class noontime car invitee. A first-class dealer. The other passengers on board the Magic Arrow have their own purposes, but Rita has been invited for a wine burger. She has a commercial purpose: to see if she can open a casino on the "Trans-European Express," which in the future will be very luxurious.

However, the Magic Arrow does not have a gambling hall. The casino is still in the planning stage, and we are not sure if the dealers will be able to deal the cards properly in mountainous areas, on rough roads, and with the vibration of the train caused by irregular speed changes. Even if they could, would the deck, field, and discarded cards collapse during the game? At Weinberger's request, Rita is in her room, silently dealing cards, continuing the game by herself, and verifying the results.

Rita is skilled in handling cards. She is not only adept at games, but also at magic tricks, fortune-telling, and all other card-based tricks, as well as counting and other forms of cheating. Although there is a rule that fortune tellers are not allowed to tell their own future, Rita has told the future of the Magic Arrow, not her own, and she has realized, albeit dimly, what has happened and what is about to happen to the train and its passengers.

While each individual comes and goes in the car with various thoughts and feelings, only Rita sits on the edge of her seat in her own room, as immobile as a mountain. Perhaps more than the witch, more than anyone else, it is Rita who anticipates all events and knows her destiny.
In Rita's own room, on the table, cards are laid out, ready for a game at any moment, and in one corner is a large cigarette case.
A girl who's kicking.

A peddler who makes a living by selling goods on European train lines. On ordinary railroads, well-equipped dining cars do not yet exist, and at best wine, ham, and cheese are sold. However, despite the inconvenience, passengers on long-distance routes are able to enjoy a reasonably comfortable trip because of the large number of peddlers. Susie is one such peddler who, like a comical hermit crab, travels back and forth along the various routes with her many wares.

She carries portable bedding for sale on her back, a variety of bread in a net palanquin, dried meat, a butcher knife, dried fish, cherries, apricots, peanuts, and mead hanging from a sash around her waist. Although all of these foods are preserved, they are guaranteed to taste good, much better than the goods in a poor dining car. The reason for the abundance of sweet foods is to relieve the passengers' fatigue. The train is not a slow-moving train, and moves around the train actively.

She is a simple girl who worships the goddess of the mountains and treats her passengers with sincerity and the spirit of a once-in-a-lifetime encounter as a peddler. Since she has been a peddler since she was a child, she knows nothing of the feelings that girls her age experience, and apart from her business-related knowledge and emotions, she has a pure heart like a maiden. She has a dreamy side, believing that one day a wonderful prince will come for her, perhaps because of this or because of the intensity of her imagination of her natural disposition.
Passenger of the first class nooner.

He is aboard the Magic Arrow as a subordinate of Luukkanen and an Imperial Intelligence Officer. An informant is expected to behave in a manner not unlike an informant. Calhill has these qualities, and has no particular characteristics or shortcomings. However, no matter when or where you meet him, you will always remember him. He has that kind of airy atmosphere.
The first thing that comes to mind is the fact that the man is a very good friend of yours. Even the most horrifying words, when spoken by Calhill, sound as natural as water seeping into the earth.
Webley-Fosbury carries an automatic revolver. Unlike Luukkanen, he can use both arms when shooting, so he wears a bayonet and a stock that doubles as a holster to increase his accuracy.
As an intelligence officer, he is not only knowledgeable about military matters, but also about the stars in the night sky.
A passenger in the observation car.
A lady with a telescope in her hand, observing the stars shining in the night sky through the glass ceiling of the observation car.

She is dressed almost bare-chested, with a hat on her head, long hair covering her face, and her eyes hidden by a mask. She is dressed as if she were attending a drunken medieval ball, but none of the passengers feel uncomfortable. It is a woman who makes those who see her think that she looks natural, as if the trees need water.
Beyond the darkness, she is familiar with the stars shining in the night sky.

cast.characterName: シャルロット・ユーティライネン
cast.originalCharacterName: シャルロット・ユーティライネン

segments.text: A passenger in a third-class hard seat car.

She is a daughter of a noble family living in the countryside. She loves reading children's literature. She was born as a descendant of witches who survived the Inquisition during the Renaissance, the early Middle Ages, and the 17th and 8th centuries.

Charlotte was born with strong magical power, the square of that of a normal witch, but she did not have the ability to use her magical power as magic. Since her childhood, she had foreseen accidents, natural disasters, and the illness and death of her friends in her daily life, but she had no means to protect them from such fate.

Unwanted magic, involuntary abilities.... Charlotte hates the fact that she is a witch. Charlotte's parents, at her own request, asked her aunt, the greatest witch of her blood, to seal all of their daughter's magical powers in a pendant.

Although the magic had been erased, Charlotte did not try to make friends, perhaps because she felt inferior. She was afraid of foreseeing the death of her friends. She simply locked herself in her room by herself and only read books.

Perhaps it was because she grew up in such a situation for so many years, but in reality, she is just a lonely and shy person. The only person she can be honest with is her maid, Mel, who has been taking care of her since she was a child. Charlotte looks up to Mel not as a maid, but as an older sister, and at the same time, she admires her as an ideal woman.
